problem:
A wooden crate of mass $14\,\text{kg}$ falls vertically downward. Let $v$ be its velocity, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the crate is proportional to its velocity and acts in the opposite direction to the motion.
At a particular moment during the fall, the crate’s velocity is $7\,\text{m/s}$ and its instantaneous acceleration is $6.3\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

What is the terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}}$ of the crate? Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the crate are the weight due to gravity and drag.

${v}_{\text{term}}=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}$

feedback.problem:
A body of mass $50\,\text{kg}$ falls vertically downward. Let $v$ be its velocity, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the body is proportional to its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k=10\,\text{kg/s}$ and acts opposite to the direction of motion.

What is the terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}}$ of the body? Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the body are the weight due to gravity and drag.

${v}_{\text{term}}=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}$
feedback.worked_solution:
Terminal velocity is the constant speed a falling object approaches as the upward resistive force (drag) grows to exactly balance the downward gravitational force.
That is, at terminal velocity (a constant), acceleration is zero, so by $F=ma,$ the resultant force is zero.

First, note that only two forces act on the body: the force due to gravity, given by the weight

$$
w=mg=50\cdot 9.8=490\,\text{N},
$$

and the force due to drag $D,$ which is proportional to the velocity (and negative since it acts in the negative direction),

$$
D=-kv=-10v.
$$

Hence, the resultant force acting on the body is

$$
F=w+D=490-10v.
$$

When the body reaches terminal velocity ${v}_{\text{term}},$ the resultant force is zero:

$$
490-10{v}_{\text{term}}=0\,⟹\,{v}_{\text{term}}=\frac{490}{10}=49
$$

Therefore, the terminal velocity of the body is ${v}_{\text{term}}=49\,\text{m/s}.$
